subject: Reserved-pool autoscale regression — OptiCart impact & remediation
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@opticart.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@opticart.com
Date: 2028-12-02T09:12:00Z
Subject: High 429s + tail latency hitting our /generate endpoints in reserved pool

Hi Rishi,

Over the last 45 minutes we've started seeing a spike in 429s and long tail latency from requests routed to our reserved GPU pool (region: us-west). The burst coincided with a marketing campaign — token throughput jumped ~3x. Our service is intermittently returning 429s and some requests time out at ~8s.

Can you confirm whether any maintenance or configuration changes were applied to our reserved capacity? This is impacting checkout personalization for a subset of users. We need a brief status and ETA for mitigation.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Park
Head of Platform Engineering, OptiCart
Attachment: none
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@opticart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-12-02T09:34:00Z
Subject: Re: High 429s + tail latency hitting our /generate endpoints in reserved pool

Elena — thanks for the flag and sorry for the disruption.

Quick update: our monitoring shows a sharp increase in queued warmup tasks for your reserved nodes and a concurrent drop in autoscaler provisioning events starting at 08:47 UTC. We're investigating a regression in the autoscaler introduced in the v2.14 release that affects reserved-pool warmup parallelism under high QPS.

Immediate actions we are taking:
- Rolling back the v2.14 autoscaler change in the canary fleet (started 09:22 UTC).
- Forcing a policy-driven warmup on a subset of your nodes to drain queues (ETA 20–30m).
- Increasing temporary burst capacity for OptiCart by 25% for the next 6 hours while we validate the rollback.

Could you confirm whether your traffic includes long-prefixed prompts or unusually high initial sequence lengths? That helps us tune warmup batch sizing.

I've filed INF-1142 and attached a short ops timeline for visibility.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-12-02T10:00:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Re: High 429s + tail latency hitting our /generate endpoints in reserved pool

Rishi / Ben — quick ops note: the autoscaler regression is causing warmup workers to be serialized for reserved pools where prefix caching is enabled. Root cause looks like a missed semaphore permission in the warmup queue consumer (v2.14). I can push a patch to restore parallel consumer loops to the canary autoscalers and kick a rapid redeploy if you want.

Ben: can you verify whether the rollback to v2.13 avoids the warmup serialization? If yes, we should push rollback straight to prod for OptiCart's pool and leave canary monitoring on for 2 hours.

Grace: please prepare a short customer-facing timeline and credit proposal. OptiCart is a high-priority reserved customer.

Marissa
Attachment: none

Date: 2028-12-03T16:45:00Z
Subject: Post-incident update and next steps — OptiCart reserved pool (INF-1142)

Elena — thanks again for your patience. Below is a concise post-incident summary, immediate remediation we applied, and our next-step commitments.

Summary (what happened)
- Start: 2028-12-02 08:47 UTC — OptiCart-facing reserved pool began exhibiting increased queue depth and elevated 429s.
- Cause: a regression in the autoscaler introduced in v2.14 where the warmup queue consumer became single-threaded for certain reserved-pool configurations using prefix cache. This caused slow warmup of KV caches and a backlog under burst traffic patterns.
- Impact: 429s and tail latency for a small percentage (~4%) of requests to your /generate endpoints during peak bursts from 08:47–10:15 UTC.

What we did (immediate mitigation)
- Rolled back the autoscaler change to v2.13 in the canary fleet at 09:22 UTC and validated warmup concurrency returned.
- Performed an orchestrated rolling redeploy of your reserved pool to v2.13 between 09:45–10:05 UTC (no further errors observed).
- Applied a temporary 25% burst increase to your committed capacity for the subsequent 6 hours to absorb remaining traffic.
- Disabled a non-critical warmup optimization flag for your tenant to avoid re-triggering the serialization while we validate the patch.

Root cause and technical detail (short)
- v2.14 introduced a refactor of the autoscaler warmup consumer which inadvertently acquired a single semaphore across all workers when prefix cache pathing was active. The consumer processed warmup keys serially, creating a head-of-line backlog for in-flight warmups. The change passed unit and integration tests but did not simulate extreme burst prefix distributions for reserved pools.

Customer impact and remediation offer
- Impact window: 2028-12-02 08:47–10:15 UTC. Estimated affected requests: ~0.8M tokens across your burst window.
- We are applying a goodwill service credit equal to 12% of December reserved capacity charges for the impacted window. Credit will appear on your next invoice unless you prefer immediate billing adjustment.

Permanent fix and next steps
- Engineering will ship a v2.14 patch that restores parallel warmup consumers and includes a new warmup concurrency SLO test harness by 2028-12-08.
- We will add a canary traffic job that reproduces high prefix-burst distributions to the autoscaler test matrix by 2028-12-12.
- Schedule: follow-up technical review with your platform team on 2028-12-06 15:00 UTC (Google Meet link: https://meet.google.com/xyz-1meet).

Attachments and evidence
- ops-timeline.csv (short timeline slice)
- postmortem-diffs.patch (patch diff with semaphore change)
- service-log-slice.txt (sampled logs showing queue depth spikes)

If you'd like us to take the credit as an immediate invoice adjustment or prefer to hold for the end-of-month reconciliation, let me know. We're also available to run a replay of your peak workload on a staging replica with the patch to validate behaviour before shipping to broader customers.

Apologies again for the disruption — we own this and will follow through on the commitments above.

Best,
Rishi
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: postmortem-diffs.patch (text/plain, 4KB)
